item.title: Snapshots of the Wild: What are trail cameras teaching us? — Sat Nov 21, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Snapshots of the Wild! What are trail cameras teaching us Saturday, November 21 | 10am – 12pm FREE Education Program for youth and families N – Core | BREG – Elective Register Here! Ever wondered what wildlife is doing when nobody is looking? Join ecoEXPLORE on Saturday, November 21 for our next Mammalogy Season Skill Session where young explorers can learn all about trail cameras, how they work, and their role in wildlife research. After learning about trail photography and investigating mammal signs outside we’ll welcome naturalist Carlton Burke who will introduce us to a furry friend! Want to dive deeper down the burrow? Adults and seasoned ecoEXPLORERS can pre-register for Mammals of the Southern Appalachians, a longer class with expert naturalist Carlton Burke from 12pm-4pm. Come investigate, discover, and learn more about mammals all day at The North Carolina Arboretum!

item.title: Bent Creek Wolf Knob Loop - 8.5 Miles, 1600 Ft EG — Mon Nov 23, 8:30 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group Back to Bent Creek. This loop starts at Rice Pinnacle parking lot, goes up to Wolf Knob and then loops around and back down Boyd Branch. This loop has some easier fire road trails along with one steep climb up and down. Some of these trails are mountain bike trails although we don't tend to see many on a Monday morning.
This is a hard hike. Expect rocky, rooty trail, steep climbs, and steep up and downhills. In fall, leaves can hide rocks and roots and make footing slippery. We will keep a moderate pace when possible (last time we had a moving avg of 2.8 mph). Please only sign up if you're comfortable with steep, uneven terrain and hiking 8.5 miles. If you're not sure, message me first and I'm happy to talk it through.
https://www.alltrails.com/explore/custom-routes/rice-pinnacle-parking-to-wolf-knob-to-boyd-branch-2f0b4c5

item.title: Craven Gap — Mon Nov 30, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0 This is a fairly undulating hike. It's narrow at first with some rocky steps and then narrow and rooty for most of the way until halfway when there's a short climb to the 2.5 mile mark. We go about 2.7 to 2.9 mph.
Well behaved dogs on leashes are welcome to attend.
When you arrive, park at the gravel lot on the other side of the road, closest to Town Mountain. You'll see some people gathering by their cars.
Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among people who are already reasonably fit. It's not an endurance hike by any means, but it is designed so we can get our hearts beating a bit while still being able to have a conversation and meet new people. When you arrive, we'll circle up and introduce ourselves briefly. There will be a person who is a sweep. This person is the person who walks last and makes sure no one gets lost.

item.title: Rattlesnake Lodge Hike — Fri Dec 4, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0 Meet at the Ox Creek Trailhead at 9 a.m. We tend to park at the 2nd and third turn off, once you turn left onto Ox Creek from the Parkway.
We'll leave for the hike at 9:10 a.m. This hike is very rocky, so it's hard on the footing. Most of the hike to the ruins of the lodge is a slight upgrade and, on the return, there is a long stretch of incline just before the hike ends. When it's wet it can be slippery.
Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among already experienced hikers. We repeat the same trails weekly so that, over time, we enjoy the beauty of each trail. We limit our hikes to two hours because many of us work and have to be somewhere else by 11:15 or so. Thus, it's not possible to wait for slower hikers. We shuttle, so if someone is slower, the group would have to wait in order to give a ride back to the starting point. Thus, the need to be on the same page with regard to hiking pace.

item.title: AI Hacks & Hops: AI Is Talking About You. Is It Right? — Wed Dec 9, 5:30 PM
item.description:
AVL Digital Nomads **AI Hacks & Hops is FREE again!** Pull out your phone and ask AI, “Who’s the best [what you do] in Asheville?” Did you make the list? Did it describe you correctly?
Your clients are asking AI who has your offering, often before they ever visit a website. In this talk, Tyler of Britt Creative walks through how AI assistants actually decide who to recommend. Here’s the surprise: your own website is just a small slice of what they read. We’ll cover the two ways businesses quietly lose in AI search, the signals that move the needle, real numbers from local businesses, and how to identify the changes you should make now. Bring your phone. We’ll test this live.
**What attendees will walk away with:**
* A clear picture of what AI says about you * Where AI really gets its info (hint: not just your website) * How you lose out to competitors in AI search * A plan for auditing & improving your AI visibility
**Event Agenda** 5:30 PM – 6:00 PM: Networking, Drinks & Setup 6:0

item.title: Weekly Critique — Wed Dec 9, 6:00 PM
item.description:
AVL Writers This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.
For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.
Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.
If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.
If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

item.title: Fishes of the Southern Appalachians — Fri Jan 15, 12:00 PM
item.description: Fishes of the Southern Appalachians with Carlton Burke Friday, January 15 | 12 – 4 pm BRN – Wildlife Core Register Here! The Southern Appalachian region is rich with a variety of fish species. These include not only the better known species of game fish that we love to catch for sport or food, but also include an incredible diversity of smaller, lesser-known non-game fish, which play an important role in the ecology of our aquatic mountain habitats. In this class we will discuss many of the fish species found in the mountain region and learn about their classification, habitat, life cycles, and their identifying features. Carlton Burke is a naturalist and educator who operates Carolina Mountain Naturalists, an educational service which offers wildlife and nature educational programs throughout western North Carolina. item.description: Winter Buds and Bark with Lauren Lampley Saturday, January 15 | 1 – 4 pm BRN – Core | BREG – Elective Register Here! Ever wondered how you can identify a tree without its leaves? All tree species have different patterns of bark and leaf/flower buds that can be used to identify them even in winter time. In this program, we will look closely at the common trees around the NC Arboretum trails and point out specific characteristics of their buds and bark so you can identify them even without their leaves. item.title: Remedy Tree — Sat Jan 30, 8:30 PM
item.description:
Remedy Tree is a Florida-based Americana band rooted in bluegrass, old-time, and folk traditions. Founded in 2015 by Gabriel and Abigail Acevedo, the group blends Gabriel’s unique perspective—born in Puerto Rico and raised in rural Florida—with Abigail’s deep old-time background. Together with Nathan Beaumont on mandolin and Isaac Taylor on banjo they create original music that feels both timeless and fresh. Since signing with Mountain Fever Records in 2024, Remedy Tree has performed at Ireland, England, and all over the Eastern US sharing stages with notable acts such as Peter Rowan, The Infamous Stringdusters, Sister Sadie, Ricky Skaggs, and The Steeldrivers. Their 2025 album Beyond What I Can See continues to gain momentum as they headline The Forest Tour in the Summer of 2026. A growing force in Americana music—deep roots, new ground.
Music 8:30-11:30pm $10 cover at the door
